verdicts.decision_note: The client explicitly assigns GPIO3 to control the software-switched 5V rail, establishing an implementation-relevant ESP32 GPIO mapping.
The local exchange resolves the target as GPIO22 and GPIO23 and reports that those mapped pins are unavailable on the ESP32-S3, creating a material mapping conflict.
The client changes the executable GPIO map by assigning 5V_EN to GPIO5, SCL0 to GPIO38, and SPI MOSI to GPIO26; scalar replacements require no separate key removals.
The freelancer specifically reports that the newly assigned GPIO26 cannot implement SPI MOSI, creating a material unresolved value conflict.
The client resolves the SPI MOSI mapping conflict by replacing GPIO26 with GPIO33; overwriting the same scalar key leaves no obsolete top-level attribute.
The message explicitly states that the client-confirmed SPI MOSI pin must change again while providing no replacement, creating a material unresolved mapping conflict.
The client assigns SPI MOSI to GPIO47 and defines the available GPIO pool and strapping-pin constraint used to judge valid ESP32-S3 assignments; no removed top-level key is required.
